issues.body: `conflicting_seen` is incremented before `head_repo != repo`, worker-ref, author, and provenance validation. The status snapshot selects worker-shaped refs but does not require the head repository to equal the target, so an external fork PR with such a ref and a head-matched DIRTY status can be counted as a conflicting "worker PR" and can produce the repo-level zero-rebase warning. The PR remains safely excluded and cannot dispatch, but the new fleet telemetry is not restricted to the population its message claims.
issues.fix_hint: Keep conflict as a signal for per-PR exclusion visibility, but increment the repo-level worker conflict census only after the unconditional fork gate (and, if "worker" is intended to mean admitted worker, after the relevant worker identity/provenance gates). Add a regression fixture for a head-matched conflicting fork row asserting that it is excluded without inflating the worker conflict census.
issues.title: Conflict census can be inflated by a fork PR

verdict.summary: The change is sound and non-vacuously tested: conflict telemetry is derived only from an explicit true value bound to the live listing head, does not alter admission or dispatch state, preserves all fail-closed gates, distinguishes the rebase lane from unrelated work, and has end-to-end snapshot coverage for resolved, unresolved, admitted, and held conflicts. One minor telemetry-integrity issue remains: the conflict census is incremented before the existing worker/head-repository admission gates, so an untrusted fork using a worker-shaped ref can contribute to the claimed worker-conflict population and trigger a misleading warning. This does not grant access or suppress a trust check, so it is not approval-blocking.
